meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (commercial law codified in the Commercial Code; corporate and financial practice also influenced by common-law-style transactional documentation)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015, as amended by Ley No. 70 de 30 de enero de 2019, establishing the beneficial-owner framework, implemented by Decreto de Gabinete No. 52 de 12 de mayo de 2021 and the supplementary resolutions of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and the Registro Público de Panamá. Compliance is also governed by the Panamanian Commercial Code and Ley No. 32 de 1927 (General Corporation Law) to the extent applicable to corporate record-keeping and registered agent duties.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly executed Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) of each proposed incorporator or authorized representative, executed outside Panama
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states, followed by certified Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence / Good Standing (Certificado de Vigencia y Registro) for each juridical shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent competent authority in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states, with sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport and sworn PEP/sanctions declaration for each director, shareholder, UBO and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notarial authority in the country of residence of the individual, or Panamanian notary for local signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for foreign documents; notarial certification for Panamanian documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD/EDD screening of all directors, shareholders with an interest above the 25% threshold, beneficial owners, authorized representatives, and material counterparties. The screening must include the OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions, UK HMT sanctions, and Panama's national AML/CFT and terrorist-financing list maintained by the UAF. PEP status, including domestic, foreign and international-organization PEPs, triggers enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation, and ongoing transaction monitoring. The incorporation package cannot proceed until the registered agent has completed the client profile and issued a written compliance clearance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Official Registry Portal and Online Services Module (Servicios en Línea, Name Reservation Form / Solicitud de Reserva de Nombre)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish is the official registry language. Corporate names may be expressed in a foreign language using Latin script, but the articles of incorporation must be filed in Spanish; any foreign-language or transliterated name must be reproduced in clearly distinguishable Latin characters and, when necessary, accompanied by a certified Spanish translation. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity and must not mislead the public regarding the company's lawful or licensed activities.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon denial of a name reservation, the applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration petition (Recurso de Reconsideración) with the Registro Público within five business days of notification, followed, where necessary, by an appeal (Recurso de Apelación) before the Director General of the Registro Público within three business days of the reconsideration ruling. The appeal must cite the reservation file number, state the grounds of distinctiveness, and, where the denial relates to a restricted word, attach the prior authorization or license of the competent Panamanian regulator. If the reservation expires before registration, a fresh reservation application must be filed; extension or renewal is subject to registry practice and payment of the corresponding fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this low-risk software-technology entity. Panama law requires every Sociedad Anónima to maintain a resident agent with a physical Panamanian address, and that address constitutes the statutory registered office. A virtual office may be used for correspondence and administrative convenience, but the registered agent's physical office must remain the jurisdictional address for service of process and statutory communications. No local employees or physical operational office are required for a non-licensed ISIC 6201 company.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5% likelihood of unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk, non-licensed technology services company with no local employees. Inspections may increase if the UAF, Dirección General de Ingresos, or the Public Registry identifies adverse red flags, incomplete UBO filings, PEP-related alerts, or sanctions-list matches.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (as amended), which regulates Sociedades Anónimas; primarily Articles 1 through 60 covering incorporation, share capital, registered office, directors, and resident agent requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Personas Jurídicas
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima (Public Deed of Incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-in capital; the Company may be formed with US$10,000 in authorized nominal capital divided into shares, with payment deferred as determined by the founding directors. No escrow account or paid-up capital certificate is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The subscription of the 10,000 common shares of the Company is accepted and the shares are issued to the founding subscriber as fully paid on this date. (2) The registered office of the Company is established at the office of the Resident Agent, located in the Republic of Panama, and such office is adopted as the statutory seat of the Company. (3) [Individual Name A] is appointed as President, [Individual Name B] as Secretary, and [Individual Name C] as Resident Agent, each to hold office until successors are elected. (4) The officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute banking forms, and file all tax and municipal registrations required for the lawful operation of the Company. All officers shall take lawful action accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Clearance and Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Personas Jurídicas (online portal: www.registro-publico.gob.pa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the name application form through the official portal or in person at the Registry, stating the proposed corporate name. Pay the statutory search fee and provide a specimen signature of the applicant attorney. The Registry checks the proposed name for identical or confusingly similar prior registrations and issues a certificate of name approval.
required_dossiers: Specimen signature of the incorporating attorney or applicant
Payment receipt for name search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as similar, submit up to three alternative names in descending order of preference. There is no appeal of the Registry’s search result; resubmission with a new name is treated as a fresh application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators appear before a Panamanian notary to execute the public deed containing the articles of incorporation and bylaws. The deed must state the corporate name, authorized capital, number and class of shares, registered office, appointment of directors and officers, resident agent appointment, and the acceptance by the resident agent. The notary must notarize the deed after verifying identity and the prior name clearance certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of name clearance issued by the Registro Público
Passport or identity card copies of all subscribers and beneficial owners
Draft public deed and corporate bylaws
Statement of acceptance by the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects in the draft deed, the incorporating attorney amends and re-executes the deed before the same notary. The notarized deed will not be sent to the Registry until all signature pages are perfected and witnessed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry Registration and Payment of State Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Personas Jurídicas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized public deed in the Public Registry, together with the official state fee payment receipt. The Registry verifies the corporate name certificate, statutory formalities, and the resident agent acceptance. Upon successful review, the Registry issues the certificate of incorporation and records the date of legal existence of the Sociedad Anónima.
required_dossiers: First certified copy of the notarized public deed
Payment receipt for state incorporation fees and stamp duty
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry raises a formal objection (razón), the attorney corrects the certified copy or attaches the required legalization and requests removal of the defect. If the objection relates to fees, pay the balance and present the updated receipt for immediate re-processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (RUC) and Start of Territorial Tax Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Impuestos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registry inscription, file the tax registration application with DGI to obtain the RUC (Régimen Único del Contribuyente) for the S.A. The Company will be classified under the territorial income tax regime, with foreign-source income generally exempt from Panamanian income tax. The RUC certificate and the registered deed are required for all subsequent banking and municipal procedures.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation issued by the Registro Público
Certified copy of the public deed
RUC application form (Form 883-1 or successor form)
Scanned passport/ID of legal representative and resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI flags missing supporting documents, submit a corrected application packet with the outstanding documents and pay any late fee. DGI’s administrative clarification request is cured by filing an amended form and obtaining a written confirmation from the respective DGI desk.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipality of Panama – Dirección de Rentas Municipales; Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) as coordinating authority for the COVID-19-era simplified online company registration only. No sectoral gaming or anti-cheat license is required in Panama
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Operating License (Aviso de Operación) and Commercial Registration Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Environmental Notification (Notificación Ambiental) for office-based software development and anti-cheat middleware services. No full Environmental Impact Study is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater or VOC point-source emissions are generated. Office sanitation wastewater must connect to municipal sewers and comply with MiAMBIENTE discharge criteria; solid waste handling must follow Law 175 of 2020, and all waste electronic and electrical equipment (WEEE) must be delivered to licensed recyclers. General VOC emissions from cleaning solutions remain below the applicable notification thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the National Civil Protection System (SINAPROC) after an on-site inspection; structural load adequacy certificate from the Municipality of Panama – Dirección de Ingeniería Municipal; and workplace health and safety registration acknowledgment filed with the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama. Official portal: DGI e-Tax (dgi.gob.pa) and the DGI electronic invoicing / Facturación Electrónica platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Panama Sociedad Anónima must be incorporated and recorded in the Registro Público with a resident agent and registered office. Following incorporation, the resident agent submits the public deed, corporate charter, registered-office evidence, and beneficial-ownership information to the DGI Registry to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente). The RUC is the single tax identity used for income tax, ITBMS, employer obligations, and digital invoicing. Foreign shareholders and directors may be non-residents; no minimum capital or local economic substance condition applies for RUC issuance, although the DGI may require a local fiscal address and an active registered agent. A foreign entity with no Panama-source activity is not automatically required to obtain a RUC, but the company should register before issuing taxable supplies in Panama or maintaining a local payroll.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide US-style check-the-box entity classification elections. A Panama S.A. is automatically a separate corporate taxpayer subject to entity-level taxation on Panama-source income under the territorial tax system; it cannot be treated as pass-through or disregarded. No hybrid mismatch or reverse-hybrid election is available. The only applicable simplification election is the 'pequeño contribuyente' small-taxpayer regime, which may affect ITBMS filing frequency and accounting burden below the relevant DGI small-taxpayer turnover threshold without altering corporate tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), Panama's VAT-equivalent transfer tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 0 — there is no general economic-turnover exemption from ITBMS registration; any person carrying out taxable transfers of goods, imports, or taxable services in Panama must register for the RUC/ITBMS. The DGI small-taxpayer regime, applicable to taxpayers with gross annual receipts below the ministerial threshold periodically updated by DGI resolution, affects simplified filing and invoicing procedures only, not the duty to register.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing through the DGI Facturación Electrónica platform. Taxpayers must transmit invoice data in real time through DGI-approved software or API integration; the DGI validates the electronic invoice and returns a unique authorization code and digital fiscal stamp before the invoice is legally issued to the client. The e-invoice must contain the supplier's and buyer's RUC, invoice series, product/service code, ITBMS rate including 0% export classification, and a QR code/digital seal. Fiscal printers are being phased out in favour of API-connected e-invoicing for all VAT-equivalent taxpayers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under the ITBMS applies to actual exports of goods that leave Panama and to services sold to non-resident recipients whose economic use and benefit occur entirely outside Panama. For the video game kernel-level anti-cheat middleware, zero-rating is claimable where the licensed software, anti-cheat updates, and SaaS/remote monitoring are delivered to foreign gaming publishers or platform operators, the servers and users are outside Panama, and no Panamanian customer receives the benefit. The exporter must be registered for ITBMS, must report export invoices through the electronic invoicing system under the export classification, and must maintain written contracts, technical documentation, user-location evidence, and banking records sufficiently demonstrating foreign-source export consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación / electronic customs manifest)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exit of goods where applicable
Commercial invoice, export contract, and purchase order identifying the non-resident buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank movement/payment evidence evidencing foreign-source export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit zero-rated export transactions and claw back any ITBMS refunds previously granted if the export documentation is insufficient, the services are deemed consumed in Panama, or the transaction is considered simulated. The typical reassessment includes 7% ITBMS on improperly zero-rated invoices, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties that may reach up to 100% of the omitted tax. Fraudulent zero-rating claims, forged export documents, or artificially structured foreign invoices also expose the entity, its directors, legal representatives, and resident agent to criminal tax-fraud penalties. The DGI generally may reassess and claw back within a five-year statute of limitations, which is extended for fraud or non-filing.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) as licensing and prudential banking regulator; Banco Nacional de Panamá as fiscal agent of the Republic; Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) as fiscal and monetary policy coordinator. Panama has no conventional central bank issuing a domestic currency; the US Dollar is legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current and capital account convertibility. The US Dollar circulates as official legal tender with the locally minted Balboa coin pegged 1:1. There are no exchange permits, prior licensing requirements, repatriation controls, or capital account restrictions on dividends, intercompany loans, royalties, or direct investment inflows. Profit remittance is subject only to territorial income tax mechanics: dividends paid by a Panamanian S.A. generally carry a 10% withholding tax when distributed, reduced to 5% if the underlying profits have already borne Panamanian corporate income tax; interest and royalties paid abroad are subject to a 12.5% withholding tax absent an applicable treaty exemption. These are fiscal obligations, not FX convertibility barriers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory surrender, forced conversion, holding period, or repatriation timeline for export receivables. Software licensing receipts may be retained indefinitely in any SBP-licensed bank in USD or other currencies. Documentary compliance under the AML framework (Ley 23 de 2015) requires the exporter to preserve underlying contracts, invoices, and wire confirmations, but no conversion ratio or Central Bank deposit obligation applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for unlicensed offshore digital EMIs operating as primary treasury rail. Panama's Ley de Innovación Financiera (2024) authorizes SBP-supervised fintech licenses and a regulatory sandbox; however, an offshore EMI (Estonian, Lithuanian, Hong Kong, or UK licensed) is not deemed a bank under Panamanian law and may not lawfully take deposits or offer corporate clearing services from within Panama. It may be used only as a secondary settlement conduit for low-value SaaS subscription receipts, subject to the debtor-side jurisdiction's own licensing regime. For the PA_CORP treasury, tier-1 licensed banks are mandatory for capital escrow, operational liquidity, and trade settlement; fintech rails are feasible only as complementary receivables collection points with immediate onward settlement to a licensed Panamanian account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid regime. Tier-1 Panamanian banks generally accept remote corporate onboarding via videoconference for low-risk technology holding structures, provided that: (i) the Charter (Poder General), shareholder registry, and corporate resolutions are apostilled and legalized; (ii) a certified Panama-qualified registered agent issues a current Certificate of Good Standing and nominee filing; and (iii) passport copies of all directors and the UBO are notarized. In practice, Banco General, BAC, and Banistmo reserve the right to require an in-person interview of at least one authorized signatory at a Panama City branch, particularly for first-time clients opening a Capital Escrow Account; Banco Nacional de Panamá and Multibank apply stricter physical-attendance defaults. No mandatory consular visit applies, but banks may substitute remote interview with an attestation executed before a Panamanian notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: association of 'gaming' or 'anti-cheat' middleware with online betting, casino token movement, or player-to-player payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product collateral demonstrating kernel-level anti-cheat and integrity middleware for licensed video-game publishers; signed software licensing agreements with identifiable publishers; SOC 2 or ISO 27001 attestation where available; written compliance policy prohibiting use of the middleware in gambling payout or real-money gaming settlement flows; and a list of customers excluding casino/betting operators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: incomplete nominee/bearer-share heritage or unverified UBO documentation for the non-resident-owned S.A.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Share Register reflecting nominative shares under Law 47 of 2013; sworn UBO declaration for all natural persons holding 10% or more; registered agent's Certificate of Good Standing; apostilled board resolution authorizing the banking relationship; and a full corporate genealogy chart covering any previous nominee shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: high-frequency inbound SaaS subscription receipts from Stripe and other payment aggregators, creating a spike pattern inconsistent with a B2B software exporter.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant settlement reports from Stripe and other acquirers mapped to individually identifiable end-customer licenses; sample subscription agreements; waterfall revenue schedule distinguishing corporate license fees from any distribution-channel receipts; and a reconciliation ledger tying gross settlement to invoiced amounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: cross-border payments to or from high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions via game distribution networks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening output for all legal entities on the counterparty list; geo-blocking declaration confirming absence of business in sanctioned territories; restricted-country clause from the master distributor agreement; and monthly transaction monitoring logs demonstrating no nexus to Russia, Belarus, Iran, Syria, Cuba, North Korea, or Venezuela.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital contributions must arrive via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the shareholder's own bank account. Field 70 (Remittance Information) should read: 'CONTRIBUTION TO PAID-IN CAPITAL OF PA_CORP S.A. - BOARD RESOLUTION [DATE]' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN - NON-COMMERCIAL - INTERCOMPANY AGREEMENT [DATE]'. Panama does not mandate a government-assigned purpose code; banks apply their internal transaction codes (e.g., capital contribution vs. service payment), so the remittance narrative must correspond exactly to the supporting corporate resolution. The bank will require: apostilled board resolution authorizing issuance of shares or the loan; updated Share Register after posting; source-of-funds letter signed by the contributing shareholder; and a bank statement of the originating account. Optional registration of the foreign direct investment with the Directorate of Investment at MICI (Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias) strengthens future dividend repatriation evidentiary files.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements and software license fidelity payments should clear via SWIFT MT103 serial wires denominated in USD; MT202 COV must be used where the ordering bank requires a cover instruction. Parent-company license royalty payments may be routed via MT103 with remittance field: 'ROYALTY/LICENSE FEE - AGREEMENT [REF] - INVOICE [REF] - PERIOD'. For large distribution agreements, a commercial letter of credit (SWIFT MT700) is permissible and advisable when the counterparty requires documentary assurance against deliverables; Panama places no restriction on LC issuance or settlement in USD. All outgoing wires must be supported by the underlying contract and invoice on file; payments to entities in Estonia, Singapore, Hong Kong, or Latvia will trigger standard correspondent-bank screening and should be filed with proving commercial documentation. USD clearing executes through CHIPS/Fedwire with 1-2 day settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (DF) booked under an ISDA 1992 Master Agreement with a licensed New York or London branch of a top-tier bank, hedged against EUR, JPY, MXN receivables from game-publisher contracts
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) on EMTA templates for BRL, COP, CLP, and ARS revenue exposure, settled in USD offshore
Cross-Currency Swaps (USD/EUR and USD/BRL) for long-term intercompany shareholder loans and IP royalty flows
Vanilla FX Options (puts/calls) permitted on a hedge-only basis pursuant to a board-approved Treasury and Hedging Policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Franchise Tax Payment and Filing (Impuesto Anual de Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% per month capped at 50%, plus monthly statutory interest; DGI blocks issuance of Paz y Salvo, and continued non-payment leads to administrative strike-off of the S.A. from the Registro Público de Panamá.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 April for calendar-year S.A.; within 3 months and 15 days after the close of an approved different fiscal period; filing is not required for a non-registered offshore S.A. deriving no Panama-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed fines for late or non-filing, monthly interest on any assessed tax, possible forced audit, and denial of tax compliance certificates required for banking and commercial operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner (UBO) Declaration and Register Update under Law 129 of 2020
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) through the licensed Panamanian registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the registered agent’s compliance calendar, in conjunction with the 15 July franchise tax window; share transfers and UBO changes must be reported within 30 calendar days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to USD 5,000 for incomplete or late declarations, suspension of registration rights, administrative sanctions against the S.A. and the registered agent, and criminal liability for wilful misdeclaration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Resident Agent Annual Address and Registered Office Confirmation, Including Corporate Register Audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed resident agent in Panama and Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuously maintained; annual review and confirmation are completed with the 15 July franchise tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of resident agent is an immediate corporate compliance failure; failure to maintain registered office details impairs service of process, invalidates certain filings, and may result in administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic audit applies to a private S.A. solely by virtue of incorporation; mandatory independent audit is triggered when the entity exceeds the net Panama-source gross revenue threshold generally set at USD 2,000,000 per annum, exceeds regulatory asset thresholds, or conducts licensed activities such as banking, securities, or supervised gaming payment operations; voluntary audit is customary for cross-border due diligence and US-style financing.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB and adopted in Panama; IFRS for SMEs is available for qualifying smaller entities; statutory books are kept in Spanish and preserved either in Panama or with the registered agent as required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 129 of 2020, every S.A. must maintain a current Ultimate Beneficial Owner register through its resident agent. The shareholders or directors must provide an annual written confirmation of UBO details, and any share transfer or UBO variation must be filed within 30 days. The registered agent records the confirmation, updates the register of shares, and files the UBO declaration with the Panamanian competent authority; failure to provide the confirmation suspends corporate administrative services.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders (Libro de Actas de Accionistas)
Minute Book of Directors (Libro de Actas de la Junta Directiva)
Register of Share Transfers and Pledges
UBO Register and Registered Agent Compliance File

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,200 per annum depending on the licensed Panamanian registered agent and level of corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 12,000 per engagement for an unlisted S.A.; higher fees apply for group consolidation, IFRS conversion, or DGI-required audited financial statements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat rate on allocable Panama-source taxable profits
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: no Panama tax on foreign-source income realized by a Panama S.A. unless the activity is located in or derives from Panama. No general software/IT tax holiday applies to ISIC 6201, but qualifying exporters in licensed regimes (e.g., Panamá Pacífico, Colon Free Zone transfer operations) may benefit from 5% to 3% regimes. For anti-cheat middleware licensing, income from software exploitation by non-resident gaming operators outside Panama may be sourced abroad and thus exempt, if the core development or server activity is not physically performed in Panama.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 745 - Declaración Jurada Anual del Impuesto Sobre la Renta de Personas Jurídicas; filed electronically via the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) E-Tax 2.0 portal (etax.mef.gob.pa).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return, accompanied by monthly/quarterly advance payment declarations where the corporate has substantial prior-year tax liability; zero-filers still submit the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year end (31 December), due on or before 31 March of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, due no later than the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registro Único de Contribuyentes and verificador digit of the Panama S.A.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain the RUC through the Panama resident agent / legal representative before filing; a foreign corporate shareholder cannot use its foreign tax identification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the taxable period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Match the official adoption in the public registry unless a formal fiscal year election was filed; calendar year is default.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Ingresos Brutos por Ventas, Servicios y Actividad en General
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue derived from gaming anti-cheat middleware licenses, subscriptions, integration services, and royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all Panama-sourced revenue. Revenue from foreign gaming operators is reportable as exempt if the contracts, servers, and core value-adding activities are factually located/executed outside Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Renta Neta Exenta de Fuente Extranjera
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income from sources outside Panama, as permitted by the territorial rule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support with executed license agreements, payment rails, invoices, and evidence of performance abroad; do not use this field for Panama-source revenue disguised as foreign-source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs and expenses attributable to generation of Panama-source taxable income, including R&D, cloud hosting, personnel, and intercompany fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate costs using a consistent business basis; intercompany charges must meet the arm’s length standard and be supported by transfer-pricing documentation where threshold applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source gross income less allowed deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the S.A. has no Panama-source activity, enter zero; do not include foreign-source licensing income or group treasury income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax at 25% on Renta Neta Gravable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No preferential rate applies to standard software export income unless under an approved Ex port Processing Zone law; otherwise the flat 25% applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Anticipos Pagados y Saldo a Pagar
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax payments made during the year and final balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit only payments made using the corporate RUC; the remaining balance must be settled through the DGI virtual payment module before the deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties include administrative fines generally ranging from B/.500 to B/.10,000 (1:1 with USD) depending on corporate size and gross revenues; late payment triggers a 10% surcharge plus monthly default interest at 1.5% (approximately 18% annualized); fraudulent omission of taxable Panama-source revenue triggers a penalty of 50% to 100% of the evaded tax and criminal referral to the Public Prosecutor.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding tax on dividends paid or credited out of Panama-source taxable profits; dividend distributions sourced from foreign-source profits can be declared as exempt from Panama dividend tax upon documentary support. For publicly listed shares or qualifying Panama Pacifico entities, reduced rates may apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced rate or exemption under a Panama income tax treaty (e.g., UK, Spain, Mexico, France, Netherlands, Singapore, South Korea), the non-resident shareholder must deliver to the Panamanian paying company a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the shareholder’s home tax authority, together with a beneficial ownership declaration, before the dividend record date. The paying company must retain the TRC and present it to the DGI upon request; if not in place, the full 10% withholding is due.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-resident lenders/creditors is generally not subject to Panama withholding tax (0% statutory); royalties and software license fees paid to non-residents for IP exploited outside Panama are also not subject to Panama withholding tax (0% statutory). If the licensing or service is deemed to generate Panama-source income, the payor may be obliged to apply the applicable 25% corporate income tax through withholding or permanent establishment accounting. Treaty rates for interest/royalties range from 0% to 10% depending on jurisdiction; a valid TRC is mandatory for any treaty reduction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. USD 5,000,000 (Panama Balboas at 1:1 with USD) of gross annual income triggers contemporaneous Transfer Pricing documentation for related-party transactions; Panama S.A. must also file the annual TP informative annex (Form 748/Anexo de Precios de Transferencia) when group-related revenue exceeds the threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama’s Economic Substance Regulations (Law 254 of 2021, Executive Decree 9/2022) apply to all legal entities performing 'relevant activities'. Software licensing and development services are a 'service business' for ESR purposes. The S.A. must prove and report: (a) core income-generating activity performed in Panama; (b) an adequate number of local employees and physical premises; (c) board meetings and management decisions in Panama; and (d) operating expenses commensurate with revenue. An anti-cheat engine business that functions solely as a shell or passive IP-holding vehicle without local substance will fail ESR.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately reclassifying Panama-sourced software revenue from gaming operators as foreign-source income; using fake foreign contracts or shell offshore IP vehicles to escape the 25% corporate tax and dividend WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI imposes 50% to 100% penalty on the omitted tax plus 1.5% monthly default interest; Panama Criminal Code and Law 8 of 2010 treat intentional evasion as a financial crime punishable by 3 to 6 years imprisonment; assets and bank accounts may be seized via administrative enforcement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, resident agents, and beneficial owners who sign false returns or orchestrate sham foreign income are jointly liable for the evaded tax, face travel bans and embargoes, and may be prosecuted personally; professional licenses of involved lawyers/accountants may be suspended.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Panama S.A. with no physical office, no local payroll, no local board meetings, no bank account in Panama, and failing to file the ESR annual return while claiming treaty benefits and foreign-source profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR penalties include fixed fines from B/.10,000 to B/.50,000, cancellation of the RUC, forced dissolution of the entity, and automatic information exchange with OECD/EU jurisdictions; the corporate veil may be lifted under Panama’s anti-abuse doctrine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The named Panama director may be fined personally for non-compliance with ESR, barred from serving on any Panama company for up to 5 years, and subjected to travel restrictions if tax debts arise from the shell structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits to the foreign parent or shareholders without applying the 10% dividend WHT, or thatched use of a fake treaty TRC to avoid withholding on Panamanian source earnings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The paying S.A. is liable for the un-withheld dividend tax, plus the 10% surcharge and monthly 1.5% interest; professional enablers may be sanctioned for facilitating unlawful non-taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize or approve distributions without satisfying withholding obligations are personally and severally liable to the DGI for the resulting deficiency; bank directors can face travel bans and personal seizure of assets when corporate assets are insufficient.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Swift wires or Stripe settlement proceeds from licensed or unlicensed gaming operators in high-risk jurisdictions without conducting CDD/KYC, filing Suspicious Transaction Reports, or maintaining beneficial-ownership records for the Panama S.A.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 23 of 2015, as amended, authorizes fines up to B/.5,000,000 per violation against the corporate; compliance officers and beneficial owners may be fined separately; criminal money laundering charges carry penalties of 5 to 15 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and resident agents who knowingly process gaming-derived proceeds from unlawful operations can be charged as principals in money laundering; travel bans, asset freezing, and imprisonment apply; directors are disqualified from future financial services functions in Panama.
